boundary_rationale: The unit opens on “The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah” (web:Jer.25.1), spliced הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֤ה עַֽל יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ (oshb:Jer.25.1, byte tier) -- a word-event header built on the preposition al (concerning) rather than el (to), doubled again in עַל כָּל עַ֣ם יְהוּדָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.25.1, byte tier), “concerning all the people of Judah.” The header carries its own date stack in the same verse (the fourth year of Jehoiakim, the first year of Nebuchadnezzar) and is followed by a third-person notice of delivery (25:2) before the voice turns first-person at 25:3: “Yahweh’s word has come to me, and I have spoken to you” (web:Jer.25.3), rendering הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלָ֑י (oshb:Jer.25.3, byte tier) -- Jeremiah's own twenty-three-year retrospective, framing an embedded citation of the call to repentance (25:5-6) that closes “Yet you have not listened to me” (web:Jer.25.7), spliced וְלֹֽא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֥ם אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.25.7, byte tier; the same verse also carries a ketiv/qere note further on, consulted but not spliced here). The row is held to the header-plus-retrospective material because the pivot at 25:8 turns from recounting past warnings to a fresh declaration of consequence.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Isolating 25:1-2 as a bare superscription, separate from the first-person retrospective that follows, was considered and set aside: the retrospective in 25:3-7 carries the row's substance and no addressee shift separates the header from the twenty-three-year account it introduces.
literature_type_guess: retrospective indictment sermon opening the cup-oracle complex, headed by a dated word-event notice

boundary_rationale: “Therefore Yahweh of Armies says” (web:Jer.25.8) turns on לָכֵ֕ן כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת (oshb:Jer.25.8, byte tier) -- a pivot into a fresh declaration of consequence (the Babylonian invasion, the seventy-year servitude, and Babylon's own eventual reckoning) after the retrospective just closed, though the speaker is Yahweh in both the neum of 25:7 and the koh-amar here, so the seam rests more on the shift from recalling past warnings to pronouncing a dated sentence than on a clean change of who is speaking. The unit runs to 25:14, whose recompense clause closes the sentence begun at 25:8. Midway, the declaration states that Yahweh will bring on the land “even all that is written in this book” (web:Jer.25.13), spliced אֵ֤ת כָּל הַכָּתוּב֙ בַּסֵּ֣פֶר הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.25.13, byte tier; the verse's opening verb also carries a ketiv/qere note, consulted but not spliced here) -- a self-reference whose scope (this sermon alone, or a wider written collection) this tiling does not resolve, and the row is held at reduced confidence on that account rather than treated as a settled hinge.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Keeping 25:1-14 as one row spanning the header through the recompense clause was considered: the divine voice does not clearly change between the retrospective and the declaration, so the pivot at 25:8 is a real but not decisive seam, and one fourteen-verse sermon unit would also be defensible.
literature_type_guess: dated judgment declaration naming Babylon's invasion and its own eventual reckoning

boundary_rationale: A private commission opens the row: “Take this cup of the wine of wrath from my hand” (web:Jer.25.15), spliced קַ֠ח אֶת כּ֨וֹס הַיַּ֧יִן הַחֵמָ֛ה הַזֹּ֖את מִיָּדִ֑י (oshb:Jer.25.15, byte tier) -- Yahweh, the God of Israel, addressing Jeremiah directly (“to me”), a scene shift from the dated declaration just closed. Jeremiah's own report of compliance follows, “Then I took the cup at Yahweh’s hand” (web:Jer.25.17), rendering וָאֶקַּ֥ח אֶת הַכּ֖וֹס מִיַּ֣ד יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.25.17, byte tier), and the roster of nations made to drink (25:18-26) runs into a command that keeps the same audience, “You shall tell them, ‘Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says…” (web:Jer.25.27), spliced וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵיהֶ֡ם כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.25.27, byte tier) -- a discourse imperative addressed to the nations already given the cup rather than a new audience, so the row treats it as the act's own enforcement clause rather than a fresh unit. The whole complex closes at 25:29's declaration that Yahweh is calling for a sword against the earth. Whether this cup vision anticipates the later nations material or stands as this sermon's own close is left open here, and the row is held at reduced confidence on that account.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the row at 25:27, where a fresh command opens, was considered: the imperative shape is real, but the addressee stays the same nations already compelled to drink, so this tiling keeps the command, the performance, and the enforcement clause together as one enacted sign rather than opening a new row on the imperative alone.

A koh-amar tsevaot onset follows at 25:32, but it does not change who is speaking from the neum-closed line just before it, so the row carries through the description of the slain at 25:33 rather than opening a new row there.

The priests and prophets lay a formal charge, “This man is worthy of death” (web:Jer.26.11), rendering מִשְׁפַּט מָ֨וֶת֙ לָאִ֣ישׁ הַזֶּ֔ה (oshb:Jer.26.11, byte tier), and Jeremiah's own defense (26:12-15) turns the verdict: “This man is not worthy of death” (web:Jer.26.16), spliced אֵין לָאִ֤ישׁ הַזֶּה֙ מִשְׁפַּט מָ֔וֶת (oshb:Jer.26.16, byte tier) -- the princes and the people answering the priests and prophets in the very words used to accuse him.

boundary_rationale: A new speaking party rises within the same hearing: “Then certain of the elders of the land rose up, and spoke to all the assembly” (web:Jer.26.17) opens the row, introducing witnesses distinct from the princes, priests, and prophets already heard. Their precedent-citation names the source directly: “Micah the Morashtite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah” (web:Jer.26.18), spliced מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י הָיָ֣ה נִבָּ֔א (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier) -- the ketiv spells the prophet's name מיכיה, read here against the qere מִיכָה֙ הַמּ֣וֹרַשְׁתִּ֔י that this splice follows, consulted but not further marked. The quoted oracle itself reads “Zion will be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem will become heaps” (web:Jer.26.18), rendering צִיּ֞וֹן שָׂדֶ֤ה תֵֽחָרֵשׁ֙ וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙ (oshb:Jer.26.18, byte tier) -- Jerusalem spelled plene here, וִירוּשָׁלַ֨יִם֙, against the defective יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ (oshb:Jer.25.18, byte tier). The elders draw the historical conclusion at 26:19: Hezekiah did not put Micah to death, so the present assembly should not put Jeremiah to death either. Whether this testimony belongs inside the same row as the princes' own hearing (26:10-16) or opens its own unit, as here, is a close call this tiling does not treat as settled.
strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding the elders' testimony into the princes' hearing as one scene (26:10-19) was considered: both serve the same acquittal, but the elders are a distinct participant group introduced by their own rising-and-speaking notice, which this tiling keeps as a separate row.
literature_type_guess: elders' precedent testimony citing Micah's Zion oracle to argue Jeremiah's acquittal
